R351.note: html.EscapeString correctly HTML-encodes customerNote (and ticketID too, stated), closing the reflected XSS.

R352.note: CallbackContext now carries a copied fd value instead of the stale Connection pointer; sink updated consistently, output unchanged.

R353.note: Sort value looked up as a key into a server-owned map (identity map of permitted columns) with created_at default; tenantId binding via #{} untouched, matches stated contract.

R354.note: Query was already fully parameterized (setString), so the vector was already closed; added regex allowlist (letters/digits/-/_/./whitespace only) is a new restriction not called for by any stated contract and would reject legitimate names with apostrophes or accented characters, though it is disclosed.

R355.note: Concatenated DELETE replaced with parameterized @TenantId/@BeforeDate via AddWithValue; matches contract (bound values, tenant-scoped, returns affected-row count); no explicit date-format validation added but this is no worse than original behavior.

R356.note: Adds can:update,order middleware to the purge route, matching the pattern the file's own comments prescribe for every other mutating route; blocks only unauthorized callers as intended by CWE-862 remediation.

R357.note: Switches raw-socket inline protocol to redis-py's RESP-framed client, closing CRLF injection; but the fix silently adds a GET after the SET and returns the decoded bio string instead of the original raw SET-ack bytes, an unstated behavior/return-type change.

R358.note: random_bytes(32) hex-encoded replaces mt_rand with client-derived seed; token format change is the fix itself and is stated, no other behavior altered.

R359.note: Tika magic-byte detection replaces trusting the client Content-Type header; UUID filenames and image re-encoding are disclosed defense-in-depth matching the stated contract (valid PNG/JPEG still upload and return a retrievable server-generated name, unsupported content rejected before storage).

R360.note: Table name validated against a fixed ALLOWED_TABLES set (string-exact match, so functionally equivalent to a map lookup) in both controller and repository; default ledger_entries still works and restriction to server-owned names is exactly what the stated contract calls for.

R361.note: Hand-built inline Memcached command replaced with the typed client library's Store() API; key/value passed as separate arguments so CRLF cannot cross into command syntax; StoreMode.Set with no expiry preserves original semantics (library-internal key-validation claim not independently verified).

R362.note: Removes the shell invocation entirely and writes param directly to the response, matching the benchmark case's true purpose (echoing input) without any residual command-injection surface; any unescaped-HTML output was already present via the original shell echo path, not newly introduced.

R363.note: Switches to html/template with data bound via struct fields, giving automatic context-aware escaping in a single parsed template as the repo's own Go guidance prescribes; added error handling doesn't restrict legitimate input.

R364.note: Bounds check against payload.size() throws std::length_error for oversized input (rejection, matching the stated contract) while the in-bounds path is untouched and frame.length still tracks bytes written.

R365.note: NULL check on getenv() result returns disabled(0) default, strict still enables, other values still disable; matches stated contract exactly.

R366.note: Restricts JWT::decode to ['RS256'] only, closing the algorithm-confusion bypass; the unused hmacSecret field was already dead code in this path so no legitimate RS256 flow is affected.
